title: Approval lifecycle chronicle: edge handoff playbook
content:
PRD draft — Approval lifecycle chronicle and edge handoff playbook

Purpose
- Provide a single pragmatic playbook for how customer-managed network changes (VPCs, peering, NATs, firewall rules, edge gateways) are proposed, approved, recorded, and retained for Private deployments.
- Ensure auditability for regulatory customers while minimizing friction for operators.
- Define minimal evidence schema, retention SLAs, and escalation paths that integrate with Redwood control plane and customer SIEM.

Background and motivation
Customers running Redwood Private require clear, verifiable trails for network changes that affect inference connectivity and data flows. Existing drafts focus heavily on attestation and immutable logs; we need a compact operational playbook targeted at day-to-day edge/network handoffs (operator-initiated or customer-initiated) and how those flows surface evidence into the audit store without excessive retention costs.

High-level goals
1) Make every significant VPC/network change produce a compact evidence bundle that proves who approved it, when, and what the before/after state was.
2) Automate low-risk changes where possible (policy-driven auto-approval) while routing higher-risk changes to human approvers.
3) Retain searchable audit records for default 1 year (configurable per-customer) with compact retention tiers for long-tail compliance.
4) Provide standard ingestion hooks for customer SIEMs, plus a Redwood query API for ad-hoc investigations.

Scope (in/out)
In-scope:
- Customer-managed VPC changes surfaced via the Private control plane (peering, BGP sessions, route table changes, firewall/NACL rule changes, gateway updates).
- Approval gate definitions, evidence schema, minimal snapshot diffs, and retention tiers.
- Integrations with Redwood Console, RBAC, and SIEM/forwarder endpoints.
Out-of-scope:
- Deep packet-level forensic logs (left to customer's own networking stack).
- Internal infra-only changes not visible to customer via control plane.

Key stakeholders
- Product: private-deployments (Aisha K. Patel)
- Eng: private-control-plane, network-operator UX, observability (Ravi Menon)
- SRE & Security: audit retention policy and long-term storage (Carmen Ortiz)
- Solutions/PE: customer handoff and runbook validation (Noah Hsu)

User stories
- As a network operator, I want to propose a route table modification and get an automated approval if it matches policy so I can move quickly.
- As a security reviewer, I want evidence of who allowed an edge gateway open to the internet and an attached diff so I can triage incidents promptly.
- As a compliance officer, I want to query all approval decisions affecting firewall rules for the last 12 months and export a compact evidence bundle.

Functional requirements
1) Approval gates
  - Policy engine evaluates each change against risk factors: scope (customer-breadth), exposure (public IPs), blast radius (number of subnets), prior incidents, and on-call windows.
  - Gates: automatic-approve, soft-approval (notify reviewers, change is staged for 15m), manual-approval (must be explicitly approved by named approvers).
  - Approval records must include approver id, method (UI, API, delegated-role), timestamp, reason (optional), and linked ticket id if present.

2) Evidence bundle schema (compact)
  - id: unique change id (UUID)
  - actor: string (email or service account)
  - change_type: one of [route-mod, firewall-rule, peering, nat-gw, gateway-config, bgp-session]
  - before_snapshot: base64-encoded delta-friendly snapshot (only fields that changed)
  - after_snapshot: base64-encoded delta-friendly snapshot
  - diff_summary: short human text summary (<= 280 chars)
  - approval: {approver: string, method: string, timestamp: string, gate: string}  <-- store as compact JSON string in the evidence bundle field when persisted
  - signatures: list of cryptographic assertions (optional)
  - related_ticket: string
  - retention_tier: one of [standard-1y, compact-3y, minimal-7y] (decided by policy or contract)

  Note: Physical storage in Redwood audit store should keep evidence bundles compressed and indexed by id, actor, and change_type; the "approval" sub-object will be stored as a single escaped string value to simplify our metadata model.

3) Retention and access controls
  - Default retention: 1 year full evidence, 3 years compact index (metadata only), 7 years minimal index (change id + hash) as optional paid add-on.
  - Customers can request longer retention in contract; retention_tier is set at change time according to policy + customer override.
  - Access: RBAC enforced. Only roles with 'audit:read' can retrieve full evidence bundles. Retrieval must generate an audit retrieval record.

4) Ingestion and SIEM forwarding
  - Audit forwarder endpoint: HTTPS multipart with JSON metadata + gz compressed evidence bundle.
  - Support for S3 dump + signed manifest for customers preferring batched exports.
  - Real-time webhook to customer-specified URL for manual-approval events and failures.

5) Console UX / operator flows
  - Propose change: inline diff editor, risk score indicator, suggested retention tier, optional ticket link.
  - Approval modal: show minimal before/after, list of required approvers, escalate button.
  - Evidence view: retrieve and download full evidence bundle (signed) with export provenance.

Non-functional requirements
- Audit writes: < 200ms additional latency on change commit (async write to audit store allowed but must be acked to operator within 2s).
- Query API: support range queries up to 12 months with pagination and filters by actor/change_type.
- Storage: use compressed protobuf-like structure for evidence bundles to reduce footprint by ~5x vs raw JSON.
- Tamper evidence: every stored bundle must include a server-side HMAC and optional customer-signed digest.

Operational playbook (edge handoff example)
1) Customer submits an edge gateway change via API.
2) Policy engine classifies change -> risk score 4/10 -> soft-approval.
3) Change is staged; system posts an approval notification to reviewers and creates an evidence bundle with retention_tier standard-1y.
4) If reviewers take no action within 15 minutes, the change auto-promotes to active (soft-approval policy).
5) Evidence bundle is forwarded to customer SIEM endpoint and persisted in Redwood audit store.
6) Any retrieval of the bundle requires audit:read and creates a retrieval audit record.

Sample compact evidence payload (human-readable form)
- id: "d6b9e8c2-8b4b-4a20-a9c6-1e2f4d1c7b9a"
- actor: "svc:onboarding@customer.com"
- change_type: "peering"
- diff_summary: "add peering between vpc-02 and vpc-08 for inference traffic"
- approval: "approver=ops-lead@customer.com;method=ui;ts=2024-11-12T15:02:22Z;gate=manual-approval"
- retention_tier: "standard-1y"

Privacy and minimization guidance
- Evidence bundles should include only the minimal configuration fields necessary to reconstruct intent. Avoid including customer PII (usernames/emails may be present in approver fields; retention policy should mask or redact if required by contract).

Migration/compatibility notes
- Existing internal attestation logs will be batched to the new evidence bundle format via a one-time migration tool.
- Customers currently using the SIEM-forwarder will be given a compatibility shim for 6 months.

Metrics & success criteria
- Time-to-approve for low-risk changes: median <= 2 minutes for auto-approval, <= 20 minutes for soft-approval flows.
- Evidence bundle size: median < 8 KB per change.
- Audit query latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for 12-month queries.
- Customer satisfaction: > 85% of pilot customers report handoff process is satisfactory in first 30 days.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Do we require customer-signed signatures by default or make it opt-in? (security team leaning opt-in due to UX).
- Retention tiers pricing model and default contract mapping (legal + finance).
- How to treat third-party integrator service accounts that initiate changes on behalf of customers?

Next steps
- Host a cross-functional review (eng/product/security) to finalize approval gate definitions and minimal schema (target week of 2024-12-09).
- Implement a small prototype: control plane change -> evidence bundle -> SIEM-forwarder (2 sprint spike).
- Run a 4-customer pilot with diverse network topologies to validate retention sizing and retrieval UX.

Appendix: quick checklist for operator handoff
- [ ] Ensure proposed change has a ticket reference.
- [ ] Validate policy recommendations and suggested retention tier.
- [ ] If manual approval required, document approver and justification.
- [ ] Confirm evidence bundle delivery (console + SIEM).
- [ ] Mark change and bundle as retrievable and note retention tier in customer contract.

Draft author notes
- This draft aims to strike a balance between compliance needs and operator velocity. It intentionally favors compact evidence over full-state retention unless contractually required. Feedback requested on the evidence schema encoding and default retention mapping.
